newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline steadies, arb bullish, crack enticing.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline steadies, arb bullish, crack enticing.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices were steady as traders balanced an open arbitrage to the United States ahead of the driving season with a crack spread that could encourage refineries into boosting their gasoline production.
Some traders also said they were cautious in selling into the market ahead of a three-day weekend in the U.K. and with a Scandinavian oil company a noted buyer this past week.
Eurograde barges were valued at $196/$197 with one trade heard at $197 fob Rotterdam and some unconfirmed talk of even higher prices toward $200.
"Today it is very quiet and people are undecided where the market is going," a trader in Germany said. "There is mogas available on the fob market."
"There is a feeling that essentially there is more than enough crude around and nice margins and usually a downward trend occurs in due course."

NWE shipped at least 200,000 to 300,000 tonnes of gasoline to the U.S. in the second half of April, traders said, but it was unclear if the strong level of exports heading into the 1996 driving season would be matched this year.
